location_address: 2661 Taylor Street San Francisco, CA US 94133
description:
Discover the majestic Muir Woods National Monument and experience the iconic Golden Gate Bridge in one unforgettable day.

Begin your adventure at 2805 Leavenworth St, where you’ll board a shuttle from Fisherman’s Wharf and cross the Golden Gate Bridge en route to the peaceful redwood forest. Spend 90 minutes walking among the towering coastal redwoods before heading to Sausalito.

Enjoy free time in charming waterfront town to dine, shop, or relax. Then, return to San Francisco on the shuttle and pick up your included bike at 501 Bay St for a self-guided ride along the scenic Bay Trail, with the option to bike back across the Golden Gate Bridge.

This experience offers the perfect mix of natural beauty and city exploration, ideal for families, couples, and outdoor enthusiasts.

If you book online, you’ll receive an electronic waiver to complete in advance. Walk-in guests will complete the waiver during check-in before the rental begins.

faq_items.question: Is Muir Woods accessible to those with limited mobility?
faq_items.answer: Yes! Muir Woods has 1.5 miles of paved or boardwalked trail which is mostly flat. Loops of half a mile, one mile, or two miles are easily achieved on this trail. It also features many benches in both sun and shade for resting. For those with a little more mobility, a dirt fire road to Camp Alice Eastwood provides a relatively easy graded additional trail. The café, gift shop, and restrooms all meet ADA accessibility standards, and six parking spaces are reserved in the main parking lot for those with disabled parking placards or license plates. There are two wheelchairs and two strollers available to borrow on a first-come, first-serve basis at the visitor center.

faq_items.question: Can I picnic in the park?
faq_items.answer:
No, the park is simply too small a space for so many people to enjoy picnicking without impacting the very forest which they are here to visit. However, there are several picnic areas nearby, including Muir Beach, Muir Beach Overlook, and Bootjack Picnic Area.

Food and hot beverages are available in the café, operated by the park concessionaire, Muir Woods Trading Company.

faq_items.question: Is photography allowed in the park?
faq_items.answer: Yes, for personal purposes. You and your camera equipment must stay completely on the trail at all times. However, if you are filming for commercial purposes, you will need a permit.

faq_items.question: What will we see at Muir Woods?
faq_items.answer: ou will see the tallest type of tree in the world, the Coast redwood, sequoia sempervirens, as well as the countless other plants and animals that are part of an old-growth redwood forest, including tanoak trees, ferns, redwood sorrel, stellar jays, black-tailed deer, and banana slugs, to name a few.

faq_items.question: Are there any dangerous plants or animals?
faq_items.answer:
Plants: We have both poison oak and stinging nettle. With poison oak, as the saying goes, "leaves of three, let them be." If you stay on the lower trails, you are unlikely to encounter either. If you will hike further in the woods, ask a ranger to show you a picture of what to avoid.

Animals: Our animals are safe for the most part, but can become dangerous if they are sick, injured, or harassed. Do not approach wildlife, no matter how small and harmless it appears. An animal that allows you to approach it is more likely to be sick and dangerous. While there have been mountain lion sightings nearby, they have not been seen in Muir Woods itself. The most dangerous animal in the park is the yellow jacket. If you have known allergic reactions to bee stings, please bring your medication. Ticks are present and may carry Lyme disease. Rodent droppings may contain Hantavirus. West Nile Virus has been detected in the San Francisco Bay Area (though Mosquitos are rare in Muir Woods).

faq_items.question: Can I take anything from the park as a souvenir?
faq_items.answer: No, everything in the park is protected, including animals, rocks, historic artifacts, leaves, redwood cones, and sticks. Take only memories and photographs, leave only footprints. Muir Woods has a bookstore and gift shop where souvenirs may be purchased.

faq_items.question: What bike should I choose?
faq_items.answer: Choosing a bike depends on the type of ride you are looking for. The most popular bike for casual, round-the-bay trail touring is the city bike. The second most popular bike is the pedal assisted E-bike. For advanced rides up to Mt. Tamalpais a performance bike is recommended, while riding through the Marin Headlands might require a MTB. Please consult our staff during check-in if you have any questions regarding your preferred route and which bike to choose, we are happy to accommodate a bike change from your original reservation.

faq_items.question: Is a helmet included with my rental?
faq_items.answer: Absolutely! California helmet law is mandatory under age 18 and for E-bikes.

faq_items.question: Will you give us a bike lock?
faq_items.answer: Included FREE with all bike rentals are: helmets, front camera bags, bells, maps & map holders, water bottle holders, bike lock, and detailed map assistance.

faq_items.question: What will the weather be like? What should I wear?
faq_items.answer: Weather in San Francisco can vary from neighborhood to neighborhood! Weather can be sunny one minute then foggy the next and it’s almost always sunny and ten degrees warmer in Sausalito! We always recommend layers: dress comfortably enough for your bike ride but also consider the variations in our weather. Also, the bikes have rear racks & Bungees to strap down any extra layers. Ponchos for rainy weather are available for purchase at our shops.

faq_items.question: Is it possible to bike on the Golden Gate Bridge?
faq_items.answer: The Golden Gate Bridge features a wide bike path on both sides.

faq_items.question: How do most people get back from Sausalito?
faq_items.answer: Most people ferry back to Fisherman's Wharf as the 2 mile downhill into Sausalito from the Golden Gate Bridge is uphill on the way out!

faq_items.question: What happens if something goes wrong with the bike during my rental?
faq_items.answer: Please call our emergency hotline, 415-346-2453. We provide an en route rescue service to fix your issue.
